title: Linear-Time T-Gate Optimization via Random Abstraction
summary: Quantum computers promise exponential speedups for problems in cryptography, chemistry, and optimization. Realizing this promise requires fault tolerance: physical qubits are noisy, so logical qubits must be encoded redundantly across many physical ones using quantum error-correcting codes. In most practical fault-tolerance schemes, T gates cannot be implemented transversally and instead require costly magic-state distillation protocols involving a complex set of operations.
